spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the read-modify-write loop the API exists for: the editor UI is generated from a real getPathData() parse and every edit runs a real setPathData(), displaying the browser's re-serialized d attribute.

interactive.rationale: Six generated numeric inputs plus reset; editing M.x to 33 changed the attribute readout from 'M 20 110 L 70 20 L 120 110 Z' to 'M 33 110 L 70 20 L 120 110 Z' and moved the rendered triangle — verified headlessly.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Card promises one labelled input per segment value with live re-serialization, which is what renders.

edge_cases.rationale: Unsupported and partial-surface builds get an honest no-editor fallback with the triangle still rendering, but the editor only ships one starting shape and does not let the visitor paste an arbitrary path (the segment-inspector covers free-form input).

references.rationale: chromestatus and setPathData spec links present.

conformance.rationale: The suite's setpathdata-roundtrip-serializes-d script assertion pins exactly this page's roundtrip contract.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 153 via Playwright CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp here): flagged run shows value names (x1/y1 per command), live d changes on input, reset restoring the original; unflagged run shows zero inputs and the honest fallback; clean console/network; both-viewport screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the roundtrip produced a non-empty serialized d per edit and the explicit fallback branch when methods are missing.

design_system.rationale: Fieldset/legend styling from variables, mono inputs on ivory with black borders, no raw hex.

accessibility.rationale: Each generated input has a visible value-name label plus a per-segment aria-label; fieldsets group segments with legends; outputs are aria-live; the preview SVG carries role=img with a label.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Inputs wrap in a flex grid with 44px min-height; 360px screenshots show no overflow and comfortably tappable fields.

openQuestions.title: Let the editor start from a visitor-supplied path
openQuestions.detail: The editor is strongest on the fixed triangle because the input count stays small, but allowing a paste-a-path flow (bounded to a sane segment count) would demonstrate the generated-UI idea on arbitrary data. Keep the triangle as the default.

guidanceConsulted.query: range slider input accessible labeling and keyboard
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Inputs need visible labels and sensible numeric affordances (type=number, step).
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Every generated input is type=number step=1 with a visible mono label naming the spec parameter (x, y, x1…).

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible status updates live region after button action
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce state changes in text near the control.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The re-serialized d readout and the action output are aria-live and update on every edit.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Prefer wrapping flex/grid tracks over fixed-width control rows.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Segment value inputs live in a wrapping flex grid; verified overflow-free at 360px.

summary: Built and verified 2026-10-25 in the weekly hardening coverage sweep. The flagged Chromium 153 run proves the full loop (parse → generated labelled inputs → setPathData per keystroke → browser-serialized d string → re-render → reset); the unflagged run proves the honest no-editor fallback. Zero console errors, zero failed requests, screenshots read at both classes.
